## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Automated analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 183 matching passages across 48 different Pali works [DharmaNexus]. The largest sharing of material occurs with both parts of the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, 46 matches in the first volume and 23 matches in the second volume) [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares standard formulaic segments—particularly across verses 25 to 30—with numerous other apadānas, including the *Uttarattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 558), *Ketakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 516), *Pāṭihīrasaññakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 435), and *Nāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 517) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus detects low-to-moderate automated alignments with Tibetan translations in the Kangyur and Tengyur, including the *Ārya-vimaladattāparipṛcchā-nāma-mahāyānasūtra* (D0077), the *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144), and the *Jātakamālā* (D4150) [DharmaNexus].
